correctness.rationale: The exact colored-noise first-intensity formula reduces to \(4\pi\) times the variance of an exponentially tilted spectral variable. Moment differentiation and endpoint concentration prove the mass identity; Gamma moments prove algebraic cutoffs. For flat cutoffs, the phase \(t u+\kappa/u^\beta\) has a unique minimizer \(u_t\) and curvature (β+1)t/\(u_t\); scaled Laplace concentration proves centered-moment convergence and the exact coefficient for every \(\beta>0\). Left edge follows by reflection. A numerical SciPy checker independently corroborates three flat exponents and the opposite algebraic edge, without being used as proof.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge originality attaches only to the sharp family of infinitely-flat-cutoff decay powers, leading coefficients, and integrated tails. Previous general intensity identities and the Paley-Wiener box special case are acknowledged. The inspected 2026 slow-spectrum theorem assumes an everywhere positive spectral lower bound and does not address compact edges; Feldheim 2011 gives an intensity formula and a box spectrum but no arbitrary β flat-cutoff saddle-variance asymptotic. A prior result could imply this after a nontrivial reduction; publication priority is not independently established.
residual_risks: A specialized older stationary-GAF or asymptotic-analysis paper may already formulate the flat-edge zero-density law after an equivalent coordinate change.

value.rationale: For the practically natural distinction between algebraic and infinitely smooth spectral cutoffs, the theorem supplies an entire sharp family of inverse-power zero-density exponents (1,2), exact edge constants and integrated tail rates, and population identification of the order and severity of flatness. This is a qualitative analytic boundary rather than an arbitrary finite slice; the result does not overclaim sample stability or a new universal intensity identity.
